cards.hook: The honeymoon ends with a lavish dinner, a conscious drink, and a todo that changes everything.

cards.headline: Still floating, but the ground is near
cards.body: The week opens in Tahaa — 4am work calls from an overwater bungalow, storms keeping you inside, Gremly's weekly summary taking shape between snorkeling sessions. By Saturday the 21st, a lavish dinner and a deliberate drink close the chapter. Not with guilt. With intention.
cards.quote: Feeling hopefully for getting back to some normalcy and the motivation I have for Gremly. Bring it on.

moments.title: Storms outside, everything held at once
moments.body: Weather pinned you inside in Tahaa and you used every hour of it — Gremly progress, Lottie animations, the weekly summary taking shape. And still: 'really loving so much time with Dave, want to soak up every last drop.' Nothing resolved. Everything held. That's the week in one sentence.

moments.title: Pride and a spiral, same paragraph
moments.body: Dave made his decision — Decagon. Your journal lit up with genuine pride, then immediately turned inward: 'if the app doesn't work I don't know what I'll do.' You caught yourself — 'it's not about me today' — but the anxiety was already out. Two people, two new chapters, one dinner reservation at Californios ahead.

threads.name: Surrogacy & Family Planning
threads.detail: A single todo — 'Surrogacy Agencies Research' — created March 15 in Bora Bora. No journal entry. No fanfare. Just a quiet start.

threads.name: Sobriety & Alcohol-Free Streak
threads.detail: March 21: lavish dinner, drinks, 'it was worth it' — a deliberate choice framed as celebration, not failure. Different from the February slip.

threads.name: Running & Half Marathon Training
threads.detail: One run logged on March 18 in Tahaa. The March 22 race day was spent exploring Tahiti before boarding the return flight to SF.

threads.name: Partnership with Dave
threads.detail: March 17 journal: 'Still feeling the love with Dave and our sex life is in a good place' — honest, grounded, present.

threads.name: App Development & Launch
threads.detail: Chat system progress, Workmaps concept introduced, weekly summary shipped — all from Tahaa, between 4am work calls and snorkeling.

threads.name: Mental Wellbeing & Negative Thought Management
threads.detail: Four consecutive completions March 10–13 — the highest streak since the habit began — with gratitude language saturating every journal entry on those days.

spotlight.title: Feeling good and breaking the promise
spotlight.takeaway: You're managing your emotional state with real skill while letting a behavioral commitment slip without acknowledgment — until March 21.
spotlight.evidence_trail: Sobriety habit: 1/21 completions this week (March 9 only), 14% cumulative rate across 21 days. Zero journal reflection on alcohol during Bora Bora or Tahaa despite multiple detailed entries. Meanwhile, negative thought management hit a 4-day consecutive streak (March 10–13) — its highest ever. Then March 21: 'had a very lavish dinner and drunk but it was worth it.' First honest integration of the tension — choosing consciously rather than avoiding the question.

research_context.title: Why this happens
research_context.body: Baumeister's ego depletion research shows that self-control draws from a shared resource — excelling at emotional regulation can reduce capacity for behavioral restraint. High-reward environments amplify this effect.
sources: Baumeister et al. (1998) — Ego Depletion and Self-Control
Muraven & Baumeister (2000) — Self-Regulation as Limited Resource
Hofmann et al. (2012) — Everyday Temptations and Self-Control

mini_discoveries.title: The 4am call reframe
mini_discoveries.detail: March 17: 'My first call of 4am sucks but I am happy to be doing it from a beautiful island' — frustration absorbed by context.

mini_discoveries.title: Work anxiety surfaces via Dave
mini_discoveries.detail: Dave's Decagon news triggered the clearest career anxiety of the trip: 'I really don't enjoy working at Dentsu anymore.'

primary.title: Don't let the half marathon just disappear
primary.body: You spent March 22 exploring Tahiti before boarding the return flight — the race almost certainly didn't happen. That's fine. But a goal with an interval training plan and a 1:40 target deserves a conscious decision, not a quiet fade. Name what happened and decide what's next.

secondary.title: Restart sobriety as a choice, not a reset
secondary.body: March 21 was deliberate and guilt-free — that's progress from February. The 3-month window ends around April 1. Decide now whether you're recommitting or reframing the goal entirely.

secondary.title: Give the surrogacy todo a next action
secondary.body: It was created mid-honeymoon with no follow-up. If it's real, it needs a first concrete step — not just a research placeholder sitting in the backlog.

cards.headline: 12 items need attention
cards.body: Most of these were created before or during the honeymoon and have been waiting patiently. Now that you're back in SF, a quick triage pass will clear the noise.

cards.intro: Sunday March 22 is a full stop: the half marathon date, the return flight from Tahiti, and the last exhale of the honeymoon — all on the same day. SF starts Monday.

highlights.title: Flight to San Francisco
highlights.prep_nudge: Journal entry already written: 'glad we spent the day exploring Tahiti.' Land, sleep, begin.
highlights.context: The honeymoon ends. 'Bring on a new lease on life in SF' — your words, March 21.

highlights.title: Half Marathon
highlights.prep_nudge: You were exploring Tahiti on race day. Decide consciously what this goal is now — defer, drop, or reset.
highlights.context: One run logged in the final week of training. The race and the return flight share the same date.

busy_day_warnings.detail: Return flight from Tahiti + half marathon date + end of honeymoon — emotionally and logistically dense.

key_themes: Half marathon dissolves into the trip
Dave's new job triggers career anxiety
Return to SF with renewed intent
